Full-Stack Software Engineer with 4+ years of production experience designing and delivering end-to-end web applications across enterprise and startup environments. Deep hands-on expertise in .NET Core, Angular, and SQL Server, with strong additional experience in React, Python, and Node.js.

Proven track record of owning entire application lifecycles — from architecture and database design through ETL pipeline implementation, CI/CD deployment, and live production support. Comfortable working across the stack, collaborating closely with product and non-technical stakeholders, and shipping reliable systems that real users depend on every day.

posts.body:
A short philosophical piece I've been sitting with: 'The Art of Starting Over.'

It's close to something I keep coming back to — that being authentic matters more than achieving. Most of what we call starting over is really just permission to be honest about what we want next.

Watch below.

Built this as a satire and ended up with a real app.

A polished, gamified wellness-app experience — daily check-ins, streaks, 'progress' charts — pointed at the most chaotic possible use case. The satire is the framing; the app is genuinely functional underneath.

Walkthrough below.

A small win from my last role I keep coming back to: we took a key Primewell Marketing Portal workflow from ~15 second response times down to under 2 seconds — about a 10× improvement.

No service rewrite, no caching layer added. Just a careful pass through the SQL Server execution plans, three new indexes on the right columns, and one query rewrite to remove a hidden N+1.

Lesson I'd share: before reaching for the bigger hammer, read the plan. The bottleneck is almost never where you think it is.

Shipped my new portfolio site this weekend after putting it off for far too long.

Stack: Astro + a single content.json file. No CMS, no database, no backend. Deploys to Vercel in seconds, edits at 11pm in a text editor.

Sometimes the simplest stack really is the right one. Open to feedback — link in the first comment.

One of the most underrated things you can do as an engineer is document the systems no one else wants to touch.

During an org restructuring at BCBS I spent a few weeks reverse-engineering and writing up three enterprise portals — Member, Broker, Provider — across frontend, backend, databases, deployments, logging, and external integrations. Nobody asked. It made onboarding faster, debugging cheaper, and ownership clearer for the whole team.

Writing it up here.

experience.company: Blue Cross Blue Shield of Louisiana
experience.summary:
Owned the full lifecycle of the Primewell Marketing Portal — an external-facing .NET Core / Angular / SQL Server application — from initial architecture and data schema design through deployment, monitoring, and production support.

• Designed and implemented backend REST APIs, responsive Angular frontend workflows, and automated Azure DevOps CI/CD pipelines, with Application Insights for observability and alerting.
• Drove a 10× improvement in critical feature response times (from ~15 seconds to under 2 seconds) through SQL query optimisation, strategic indexing, and caching, significantly improving user experience and self-service adoption.
• Enabled increased customer self-service and reduced support load by delivering intuitive workflows and AI-assisted features that minimised errors during plan selection and member registration.
• Collaborated directly with product, marketing, and business stakeholders to translate loosely defined requirements into implementable features, helping the team transition toward a structured Agile workflow.
• Supported the application across live production environments including on-call rotations, weekend releases, incident triage, and hotfixes, resolving deployment failures, API issues, data inconsistencies, and user-reported defects.

Systems Documentation & Platform Analysis Initiative
• Proactively led a self-initiated documentation effort during organisational restructuring — reverse-engineering and fully documenting three critical enterprise portals (Member, Broker, and Provider) across frontend, backend, databases, deployments, logging, and external integrations.
• Produced structured, cross-functional documentation that accelerated onboarding, improved debugging efficiency, and clarified system ownership across engineering and leadership teams.
• Designed and implemented a data mapping pipeline for the Vantage → Blue systems migration, transforming and reconciling provider claims data from a legacy database schema to a restructured target schema — ensuring data integrity, field-level accuracy, and continuity of claims processing across platforms.

• Developed and maintained full-stack .NET Core / Angular web applications serving 1,000+ customers, integrating responsive front ends with ASP.NET Core back-ends and SQL Server databases.
• Built and automated CI/CD pipelines using Azure DevOps, Docker, and Kubernetes for consistent, reliable cloud deployments across environments.
• Supported the full SDLC from requirements analysis through production deployment under Agile and waterfall methodologies, collaborating with cross-functional teams on maintainable multi-layered architectures.

• Resolved 100+ monthly technical support requests across hardware, software, and network issues in a university-wide domain environment.
• Built and deployed a Python-based automated ticket alert system that reduced missed support requests to near zero, improving team responsiveness to incoming incidents.
• Configured and hardened workstations end-to-end including system setup, security remediation, and malware removal, strengthening overall IT security posture.
